Instead of making minor tweaks to an already excellent game, this RPG packs in so much content that it feels like a completely new game. Some features of Persona 5 Royal are things you'd expect to see in any "director's cut" game, such as more voice acting in either English or Japanese during key story moments (players have the option of choosing which they prefer at the start). Older cutscenes have been re-edited to include new characters and events, further fleshing out the game's plot. There's even an extra school semester that significantly expands the gameplay by adding new holidays, events, and exams. That would suffice in most cases, but it only scratches the surface. There are new characters to interact with (and get to help you in your adventure), as well as a new location called Kichijoji, which includes a sports bar where you can play pool and darts with your Phantom Thief friends, a jazz bar where you can hang out and invite people, and clothing stores where you can sell off gear to collect in battle. It's a place you'll want to visit again and again. Similarly, the Thieves Den feature provides you with a space full of unlockable content such as new music, character models, artwork, and more. It even includes challenges that you can complete simply by playing the main story and side missions, as well as a card game.

Dungeons have also been significantly improved, thanks to a grappling hook feature that can be used to reach hidden areas or even ambush opponents from afar. Some dungeons have new layouts, including items called Will Seeds in off-the-beaten-path areas. When the entire set of these items is collected, they will restore your magic points and provide significant bonuses. Momentos, the randomised dungeons, have also been improved, with larger levels and an in-dungeon store that can provide bonus experience, money, and items while exploring these areas. And for Persona 5 veterans, restocking your ammo after each fight means you no longer have to save your ranged weapon attacks during a mission, making them far more useful. If there is a disadvantage to Royal, it is that there are so many things to do and so many options presented to you, especially once your group grows beyond four members, that it can be difficult to figure out what activity you should do when and with which characters. However, Persona 5 Royal is so large that you'll enjoy immersing yourself in it (or reintroducing yourself to its gameplay) for dozens of hours.

10/10

[h1]Persona 5 Royal: A Masterpiece in Gaming[/h1]

[b][u]Introduction[/u][/b]

In the ever-evolving landscape of video games, certain titles stand out as exceptional pieces of art, combining gripping narratives, innovative gameplay mechanics, and stunning visuals to create an immersive experience. Among these, Persona 5 Royal unquestionably claims its spot as one of the best video games of all time. Released as an enhanced version of the critically acclaimed Persona 5, this game transcends its genre and captivates players with its compelling story, intricate characters, and refined gameplay mechanics.

[b][u]Narrative Brilliance[/u][/b]

At the core of Persona 5 Royal's excellence lies its narrative brilliance. The game takes players on a rollercoaster ride through the vibrant streets of Tokyo, intertwining the supernatural with the mundane aspects of daily life. The protagonist, a high school student codenamed Joker, becomes entangled in a web of corruption and conspiracy as he and his group of Persona users, the Phantom Thieves, strive to reform society by 'stealing the hearts' of the corrupt evildoers in the world. The story unfolds in a series of meticulously crafted arcs, each delving into the lives of the main characters and exposing the dark secrets that bind them.

One of the standout features of Persona 5 Royal (and the Persona franchise in general) is its ability to address complex and relevant social issues. The game fearlessly tackles topics such as societal expectations and pressure, corruption, the impact of technology on personal relationships/the world around us, and even heavier themes such as mental health issues, sexual assault, suicide, and more. This narrative depth elevates Persona 5 Royal beyond a mere gaming experience, turning it into a thought-provoking exploration of contemporary societal challenges and social commentary.

[b][u]Characters and Relationships[/u][/b]

Persona 5 Royal boasts a cast of very memorable characters, each with their own unique personalities, backgrounds, and struggles. The game successfully establishes a deep connection between players and the characters, as their growth and development are intricately woven into the overarching narrative. The 'Confidant system' (a.k.a The Social Link system), a mechanic that popuralized the Persona franchise and that has been everpresent since Persona 3, allows players to build relationships with these characters; providing emotional depth, personal memories with said characters, and tangible gameplay benefits, up to a maximum "Confidant Rank' of 10. It also happens to be the case that 10 different unique Romance paths can be unlocked and explored, even simultaneously (although this can get messy, and I would not recommend it, especially so to the faint of heart and those with a good conscience).

Another selling point for this game is that the characters and cast feel very believable and 'alive', making for a that much more immersive experience. The top shelf, high quality, and realistic voice acting (both available in Japanese or English, although I recommend playing with English dub to any non-native-level-Japanese speaking player) sells these characters so extremely well and really makes you forget that you are playing a game or even looking at a piece of fiction in the first place. Because of this you're *right there* with these characters in the present moment, and you unavoidably grow fond of them the more personally you get to know them; and the more endeavours you undertake and overcome together.

The enhanced Royal version of Persona 5 also brings with it the inclusion of new characters, such as Kasumi Yoshizawa and Takuto Maruki, who add further layers to the narrative, introducing fresh perspectives and dynamics to the already established cast of characters, and besides this other characters were given additional screentime in this version of the game as well. The well-crafted character arcs, the humor that every character brings in their own way, and the emotional impact of their personal stories contribute significantly to the game's universal acclaim.

[b][u]Incredibly Aesthetically Pleasing Design[/u][/b]

Persona 5 Royal is a visual feast that combines a distinct art style with a vibrant color palette. The game's unique blend of Anime, cel-shaded graphics and stylish character designs creates a visually stunning world that sets it apart from other videogame titles. The attention to detail in the level design; which is based on real-life locations in Japan that have been recreated in-game in an almost 1:1 fashion, the beautiful and lively Anime cutscenes, the designs of the Personas -  the manifestation of characters' inner selves - are also a treat to the eyes, and above all the imaginative settings of the 'Palaces' that you and your crew have to traverse through all contribute to the game's aesthetic appeal.

Moreover, the game is accompanied by a phenomenal soundtrack composed by the fantastic composer and music artist Shoji Meguro. The game's music and Original Soundtrack do not only enhance the atmosphere, but also becomes an integral part of the overall experience. The jazzy tunes and energetic beats, and above all the lead singer Lyn's super unique and smooth voice perfectly complement the game's stylish aesthetic; creating a synergy that further immerses players in the captivating world of this unforgettable masterpiece.

[b][u]Gameplay Mechanics[/u][/b]

The addition of new personas, confidants, game(play) mechanics, and locations expands the game's scope; providing players with even more content to explore than ever before. The revamped dungeons, known as Palaces, offer improved mechanics and challenges, keeping the gameplay engaging and dynamic for returning players and newcomers alike.

The inclusion of the Thieves' Den, a customizable hub for players to showcase their achievements and interact with the game's lore, adds a layer of personalization to the experience. These enhancements demonstrate the developers' commitment to delivering a polished and well-rounded fresh gaming experience for both returning players and new players alike.

Most of all, the game simply has an astounding amount of (gameplay) mechanics. When you're not saving the world, you can do things like read a book, hit a few homeruns in baseball, study, go out on a date, do fitness, go shopping, fishing, go to the arcade, watch a movie with someone, etc. But in the palaces, you're busy with stealth, planning, item management, and strategic turn-based combat. You feel like you're truly transported into the game's world because of the sheer amount of things you can do in it.


[b][u]Conclusion[/u][/b]

I absolutely recommend this game to anybody who can appreciate a videogame that has a fantastic memorable cast of characters, doesn't mind tons of dialogue to read/listen through, loves snappy, stylish and strategic turn-based combat, can really appreciate a good original soundtrack to listen to for days on end, loves an emphasis on a truly marvelously stylish artstyle, likes Anime, and can tolerate a game with extremely hype moments that are offset and juxtaposed with many moments of slow burn/some grinding here and there.

Persona 5 Royal stands as a testament to the potential of video games as an art form. Its narrative depth, well-developed characters, stunning design, and extensive gameplay mechanics collectively contribute to its status as one of the best video games of all time. The game's ability to tackle relevant social issues while providing an immersive and enjoyable experience cements its place in the pantheon of gaming masterpieces. Persona 5 Royal is not merely a game; it is a work of art that transcends the boundaries of its medium, leaving a truly indelible mark on the hearts of players worldwide. [i]Pun intended.[/i]

This is the first Persona game I’ve played, and while I have some criticisms (mainly related to the game’s length), I mostly enjoyed it, so I’ll probably play the others at some point.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

•	Each criminal related to the main story has a “palace” within the metaverse, which takes a different form, such as a bank, museum or casino, depending on how they view the real world. Each palace contains several floors which you’ll need to explore, fighting a variety of monsters along the way, in search of the criminal’s treasure. Successfully stealing their treasure will cause them to confess their crimes in the real world.

•	You’ll also need to progress through Mementos, which is a separate dungeon containing dozens of floors, to defeat enemies relating to side quests.

•	Combat is turn based. Your party of four characters can attack enemies with melee and ranged weapons, and several different types of magic including fire, ice, wind, lightning, psionic, curse, nuke and bless. You can also heal and resurrect allies, and buff/debuff stats such as attack, defence and elemental resistance.

•	Most enemies will be strong or weak against specific elements. Attacking an enemy’s weakness will temporarily stun them, allowing you to perform a baton pass move, which lets a teammate take the next turn with increased damage.

•	When all enemies are stunned, instead of killing them you can talk to them, giving Joker the chance to acquire a new persona with different abilities.

•	While each of the seven companions specialise in specific skills and elemental attacks, Joker can switch between multiple personas during battle, which in theory gives you access to every skill whenever you need it. Unwanted personas can be fused together to create a new, more powerful one.

•	Playing on normal difficulty, most of the combat encounters felt quite easy. If you sneak up on enemies to ambush them, allowing the Thieves to attack first, and take advantage of weaknesses and baton passes, most fights can be won on turn 1 before the enemy even gets a chance to do anything.

•	Bosses, and regular enemies which appear later in the game, can be more challenging, either because of having no weaknesses, more health, or special rules. One boss in particular provides a massively frustrating difficulty spike because of poorly designed mechanics. I’m not going to go into full detail, but lets just say it relates to infinitely respawning minions and a strict time limit.

•	Outside of combat, you’ll live Joker’s life one day at a time over the course of nine months. Each day is divided into morning, after school and evening.

•	In the morning you’ll attend classes, and you actually have to remember what they teach you, because there are exams where you’ll need to answer multiple choice questions to help Joker get good grades.

•	After school and during the evening you can spend time on various activities with companions and other allies to progress their side stories and level up their bond with Joker, which unlocks new abilities, passive bonuses, and increases the power of persona fusing. However, most days you can usually only hang out with 1 or 2 people, so you’ll need to prioritise your favourites.

•	There are around 20 allies, most of which have 10 levels, and you often need to hang out with them 2-3 times per level up. This feels unnecessarily grindy considering the length of the game, and should definitely have been streamlined to save time. And even though I didn’t waste any time slots, I wasn’t able to finish several interesting allies’ storylines before the end of the game, which is disappointing.

•	In addition to all of this, you can spend your free time working part time jobs to earn cash, or read books, watch DVDs, play video games, and play darts and baseball minigames to increase social skills. Oh, and maybe you should find time to study to increase knowledge ahead of those exams.

•	[spoiler]It turns out that I also missed the chance to play an extra chapter which is unlocked by getting maximum bond with a specific character. I completely ignored him because honestly I thought he was really boring and I decided to spend my limited time with more interesting characters. Yes, the game warns you that he’ll leave school by a certain date, but I didn’t realise he was that important. I don’t think its good game design to lock content behind something that’s easy to miss, however it might have been a blessing in disguise, because I’m not sure I would have survived several more hours. [/spoiler]

[h1]Story[/h1]

•	Story is mostly great, and features lots of interesting characters. Students interested in modelling, athletics, and art, other allies such as a doctor, teacher, fortune teller, shogi player, and a Phantom Thieves fanboy. And the criminals, whose crimes are based on the seven deadly sins. I won’t spoil anything, but the first chapter focuses on a school teacher who is abusing students, and other chapters have similarly powerful themes.

•	Main story features excellent voice acting, however most of the side stories are text only.

•	I like how the game automatically progresses from one important scene to the next. You don’t have to waste time walking around from one location to another between conversations, which keeps the story flowing.

•	Eventually the game’s length starts to hurt the story. For me it was around the 70-80 hour mark. After this I started to lose interest in new twists and characters, and just wanted to get to the end.

•	The more I played, I also started to see examples of characters having multiple conversations about things we’ve already discussed, or scenes where companions got together for an update on the main story when nothing important had changed yet. Again, I feel like the script could have been streamlined by several hours.

[h1]Technical[/h1]

•	It took me 120 hours to finish the game, which provides exceptional value for money at any purchase price, but also eventually hurts the quality of gameplay and story.

•	Music is fun and stylish, I don’t think I’ve ever heard anything quite like it in a game before, but I also wish there was a larger variety of tracks, especially for combat, because the same songs repeat countless times over the course of the game.

•	I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes or framerate.

•	Controls worked great on my xbox 360 gamepad.

[h1]Recommendation[/h1]

Persona 5 is a really good game, which I definitely recommend to players who want a high quality story with interesting characters. But I do have some mixed feelings. I definitely enjoyed large parts of it, but its simultaneously too long, while not giving you enough time to do everything. I’m glad I played it, but at times it was exhausting.

[h1]Persona 5 Royal[/h1]
[h2]A Super Linear Yet Stylish Masterpiece[/h2]

Persona 5 Royal is one of the most stylish, well-animated, and engaging turn-based JRPGs out there. While it is super linear in structure, it makes up for it with an incredible story, fantastic characters, and satisfying gameplay. Whether you’re here for the deep combat mechanics, the beautifully animated cutscenes, or the dating sim elements (yes, you can romance some absolute waifus), this game delivers in spades.

Super Linear, But That’s Not a Bad Thing:-
If you’re looking for an open-ended RPG where you can make major choices that drastically change the world, Persona 5 Royal is not that game. It follows a set narrative, and you go through the same sequence of events no matter what. However, the magic is in the details—how you manage your time, the relationships you build, and how you progress in combat all feel personal to your journey. The game is strict with its calendar system, meaning every day is planned out, but it adds to the immersion of living a double life as a high school student by day and Phantom Thief by night.

Gorgeous Animated Cutscenes & Stylish Visuals:-
One thing Persona 5 Royal does better than almost any other JRPG is its presentation. The game oozes style in every frame, from the slick UI design to the flashy battle transitions. The animated cutscenes are top-tier, looking like something straight out of an anime. Even normal dialogue scenes feel alive thanks to expressive character portraits and dynamic camera angles.

Joker – The Silent Protagonist Done Right:-
The main character, known as Joker, is a mostly silent protagonist, but he still manages to have a strong presence. His design is sleek, his Phantom Thief outfit is badass, and his ability to wield multiple Personas makes him feel like a true leader. Unlike some blank-slate RPG protagonists, Joker has enough personality (especially in his confident smirks and rebellious actions) to make him feel compelling while still allowing the player to project themselves onto him.

Hot Ladies & Romance Options:-
Now, let’s talk about one of the best parts of the game—the romance options. Persona 5 Royal has some of the best waifus in gaming, and you can actually date them. From the fiery and athletic Ann, the elegant and mysterious Makoto, the artistic and quirky Kawakami (yes, your teacher), to the mischievous and playful Takemi, there’s someone for everyone. The game lets you pursue one love interest or go full harem mode (though beware of Valentine’s Day consequences). The romance is well-written, with each girl having unique interactions and heartfelt moments.

Turn-Based Combat That Feels Amazing:-
Turn-based combat in RPGs can sometimes feel slow or outdated, but Persona 5 Royal makes it fast, fluid, and satisfying. The One More system, which lets you chain attacks when you hit enemy weaknesses, adds a strategic layer that keeps battles exciting. The Baton Pass feature allows for smooth combo chaining between characters, making fights feel more dynamic. On top of that, each character’s Persona gives them unique skills, and Joker’s ability to switch Personas makes him a versatile powerhouse.

Final Verdict:-
While Persona 5 Royal is super linear, it doesn’t feel restrictive. Instead, it delivers a beautifully animated, stylish, and engaging experience that keeps you hooked from start to finish. The characters are lovable, the romance options are top-tier, and the turn-based combat feels polished and satisfying. If you love anime aesthetics, deep JRPG mechanics, and a bit of waifu collecting, this game is a must-play.
